calls.head: Stützle gets company tonight
calls.body: At home, the Golden Knights keep sending Karlsson’s line (Howden, Karlsson and Holtz) out against opponents’ first lines, far more often than chance would suggest. Ryan Craig has been using this group as a checking line on the other team’s top line. Tonight the Senators’ first line is Zetterlund, Giroux and Stützle.

surprises.body: Ottawa’s shots at 5-on-5 had a 3.9% chance of scoring on the average shot, against their usual 6.6% (about 6.4% against Vegas) and a league average of 6.3%. A team strays this far about once every 60 games.

story.head: The Golden Knights beat the Senators
paras: Braeden Bowman struck first for the Golden Knights on the power play with 11 seconds left in the second. It was a busy third period. Shane Pinto tied it up for Ottawa on the power play just 34 seconds into the period, but that was the last goal the Senators would get. Raphaël Lavoie, in his 27th NHL game, scored his first NHL goal, set up by Nic Dowd, midway through the period to put the Golden Knights back ahead 2-1. William Karlsson added the empty-netter with two minutes left to make it 3-1, and Jack Eichel added an empty-net goal with just seven seconds left to make it 4-1. Ville Heinola made his Golden Knights debut, after six seasons with the Jets, and picked up an assist.

The chances were closer than the score. Adin Hill made 25 saves for the Golden Knights, and Jonas Johansson stopped 25 of 27 at the other end. The Knights improved to 9-4-1 and climbed into first in the Pacific, while the Senators fell to 8-5-0, slipping to third in the Atlantic.

items.text: The Golden Knights won for the first time in four games.
Mitch Marner has a point in eight straight games.
Tim Stützle’s point streak ended at four games.
Warren Foegele faces his old team, Los Angeles, on Thursday.
